note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a Nationality Act B.E.2508 (1965) 10(4), 11; A06b Nationality Act B.E.2508 (1965) 10, 12, 5; L05 THA 17(2), 19(2), 19(6)): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: Parental residence restriction) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory only on the condition the dataset states; by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Thailand, 2024
sources.said: An applicant has had a domicile in Thailand for a consecutive period of not less than five years until the date of filing the naturalisation application. This timeframe is not required for persons who: render distinguished service to Thailand, are the child, wife, or a naturalised or restored Thai citizen, used to have Thai nationality, are the husband of a Thai citizen. ... n.a. ... Person naturalises in another country (loss becomes effective upon publication in the gazette) ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Thailand to a Thai citizen. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born abroad to a Thai citizen. ... Parental residence restriction ... A person is born in Thailand to both foreign parents holding a permanent resident permit in Thailand and not enjoying diplomatic immunity nor representing another country. Note: A person born in Thailand to foreign parents with temporary immigration status or illegal immigrants falls is subject to additional regulations set by the Cabinet, for which the Minister of Interior will approve Thai nationality for each particular person. That additional regulation usually depends on Thailand's policy at a particular time (e.g. the policy to solve statelessness and to assimilate the children born to former forced migrants, refugees and migrant workers). ... No provision
